messages:
Jordan: Heads-up — noticed incident-bot didn't fan out pages for the payment-p99 alert during the spike. No one got paged at 12:03 UTC.
Riley (oncall): seeing same — monitoring shows alert fired at 12:03 but no pager activity.
Jordan: incident-bot posted into #alerts but it didn't trigger the paging workflow. Quick glance at the router logs show paged-router returned OK but fanout_count was 0.
Mei: can you paste the incident-bot / paged-router logs?
Jordan: logs pasted below:
```
[2025-02-02T12:03:01Z] incident-bot -> POST /services/paged-router 200 OK
[2025-02-02T12:03:01Z] paged-router -> pager-bridge 202 queued
[2025-02-02T12:03:02Z] paged-router -> pager-bridge: accepted but fanout_count=0
[2025-02-02T12:03:02Z] paged-router WARN: routing-table-watch stale (last update 00:14:22 ago)
```
Sam: "routing-table-watch stale" — that watch logic got refactored last week (shard reconciler). Could be a regression in the watch handler.
Nina: that would explain it: router short-circuits when it believes there are no active endpoints, returning success but not fanouting.
Riley (oncall): immediate mitigation: we need manual pages while we fix router. Runbook fallback: `/playbooks/paging/fallback` -> `curl -X POST https://pager-api.company/pager/fallback -d '{"alert":"payment-p99"}'`
Mei: Kicking manual pages now.
deploy-bot: [12:10] deploy triggered: paged-router v2.1.4 -> v2.2.0 (hotfix)
Jordan: Manual pages went out at 12:11, Riley acknowledged.
Sam: initial root-cause hypothesis: the consul/watch handler in paged-router crashed silently on a NPE in the reconciler after the refactor; healthcheck still returned 200 so k8s didn't restart it.
Nina: metrics show a spike in reconciler errors at 12:02. Correlates with the alert.
Mei: pushing a quick patch to treat stale watch as transient error and return 5xx so k8s will restart pods if watch fails. Also adding defensive null checks in the reconciler.
deploy-bot: [12:18] paged-router rolled to v2.2.0 (hotfix) — pods restarted.
Riley (oncall): paging resumed after restart. Confirmed three replayed pages delivered to oncall.
Jordan: Customer impact summary: some customers experienced missing on-call paging for ~8 minutes (12:03–12:11 UTC). No API data loss or job failures reported, purely alerting gap. CS informed and tracking impacted accounts.
Sam: Follow-ups: open postmortem, add synthetic probe for routing-table-watch freshness, alert on fanout_count==0 for paged-router, revert/expand tests around the refactor, and add unit coverage for reconciler null paths.
Nina: Created ENGINFRA-4523 with attached logs/traces and timings.
Riley (oncall): Assigning remediation owners: Sam -> code fix & tests, Mei -> runbook update and add manual playbook snippet, Nina -> follow-up ticket owner and CS liaison.
Jordan: Thanks everyone. I'll drop a short incident summary into #postmortems and link ENGINFRA-4523. :thumbsup:
